entries.name: The Hark
entries.blurb: Tall, eyeless, ears like cupped hands. It does not see. It listens.

facts.text: Eyeless. It turns toward sound, not light.
A thrown tin pulled it away from the path. It goes to where the noise was, not to where you are.
Very loud noises make it recoil for a moment. That moment is a door's width of safety.
A slow, careful step does not carry. It passed within two tiles of me and did not turn.
It cannot turn a lock. It will pound a locked door until the wood gives, though.

entries.name: The Stillwatch
entries.blurb: Pale, narrow, patient. It sees only what is lit, and stops dead when a beam finds its face.

facts.text: It noticed me only because I was lit. A shuttered lamp and a dark corridor are the same as nowhere to it.
A beam on its face freezes it in place. Look away and it moves again.
Too long in the beam and it shies away for a while. The beam is not free: it spends battery.
It cannot open a closed door. A shut door is the same as a wall to it.
It will not cross the light of a Lantern Ward.

entries.name: The Understudy
entries.blurb: A figure in a coat that fits slightly wrong. It reads the rooms you leave behind and learns where you like to hide.

facts.text: It notices a door that is not how it left it, and goes to see who moved it.
Room by room, corners and hiding places first, then the next room along. It never skips a cupboard.
It checks the places I hide most often before the rest. Repeating myself is what it feeds on.
Emptied cabinets and torn open drawers are a trail it can follow.
A locked door stops it. It will look for another way round.
